title: The Bosphorus Brief: Oil Deals, a Wildfire, and a Wait for Kavala
overview: A regional energy realignment is unfolding as Turkey deepens ties with both Syria and Iraq, even as a wildfire in western Turkey and continuing Iran-Iraq strikes keep safety questions front of mind. On the legal front, the ECHR has finally set a date for its long-awaited Kavala ruling, and Montenegro's visa policy shift is worth noting for anyone with Balkan travel plans.
body: Turkey's central bank signed a lira deposit account agreement with Syria's central bank, a technical but notable step in normalizing financial ties between the two countries. Separately, Turkey and Iraq signed five agreements, including a proposal for Iraq to supply Turkey with up to one million barrels of oil daily, following the expiration of the old Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline pact. For residents, this is mostly background economic news, but it signals warmer official relations with both neighbors — worth watching if it eventually affects fuel prices or cross-border banking access.
